title: Finite group quotients preserve relative projectivity
statement: Let $B$ be a Noetherian scheme quasi-projective over an affine Noetherian scheme, and let $V\to B$ be quasi-projective of finite type. Quasi-projective means admitting a locally closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the base. Let a finite group $H$ act on $V$ over $B$. Then there exists a categorical geometric quotient $q:V\to Q=V/H$ in schemes. The morphism $q$ is finite and surjective, its geometric fibres are the orbits, $\mathcal O_Q=(q_*\mathcal O_V)^H$, and $Q\to B$ is quasi-projective of finite type. If $V\to B$ is projective, then $Q\to B$ is projective in the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective]. If $V$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], then $Q$ is integral. Restricting to any $H$-invariant open of $V$ gives its quotient as the corresponding open of $Q$. Finite morphisms and finite type are as in [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Categorical means that every $H$-invariant morphism from $V$ to a scheme factors uniquely through $q$.

source.place: WANTED locally. Rydh, Existence and properties of geometric quotients, arXiv:0708.3333v2, Theorem 4.4, Proposition 4.7, Remark 4.9, pp.20--23 (read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0708.3333). The ample-base hypothesis ensures that projectivity also has the finite-projective-space meaning.

proof.text: Choose an affine Noetherian scheme $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ over which $B$ has the stated finite projective-space immersion $B\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_S$. This immersion is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft]; it is quasi-compact because every open of the Noetherian scheme $B$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], so it is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The projection $\mathbf P^m_S\to S$ is proper [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], hence of finite type, so $B\to S$ is of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], and so is $V\to S$. By [lem-per-quasiprojective-affine-composition], the composite $V\to S$ has such an immersion too. Apply [lem-per-equivariant-projective-envelope] to obtain an equivariant open immersion $V\subset M=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ with $A$ a graded quotient of a polynomial ring over $R$, generated in degree one. Put $R_0=A_0$; this is a quotient of $R$, and $H$ fixes it. Write $C=A^H=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}(A_n)^H$, so $C_0=R_0$. The equality of graded components follows by applying each $h$ to the unique homogeneous decomposition of an invariant element.

source.place: Tag 0C4M; constructions.tex Tags 01WD, 03GL; affine homogeneous version of Rydh Proposition 4.7.

proof.text: For each degree-one generator $a_i$ of $A$ over $R$, the orbit polynomial $\prod_{h\in H}(T-h(a_i))$ is monic with coefficients in $C$ and vanishes at $a_i$. Let $e=|H|\geq1$. Reducing powers with these monic relations shows that the finitely many monomials $\prod_i a_i^{j_i}$, $0\leq j_i<e$, span $A$ over $C$: induction on the total degree of a monomial reduces any exponent at least $e$. Apply [lem-per-artin-tate-subalgebra-finite-type] to $R\to C\subseteq A$. It gives that $C$ is of finite type over $R$, hence over $C_0=R_0$. Replacing a finite generating family by its finitely many homogeneous components gives homogeneous generators: all those components are invariant because the action preserves degrees. The injective graded extension $C\subseteq A$ is therefore module finite and satisfies every hypothesis of [lem-per-finite-graded-proj-morphism]. Obtain a finite surjective map $r:M\to P=\operatorname{Proj}(C)$ with the stated standard-open chart maps.

source.place: Tag 00IS (lemma-Artin-Tate); constructions.tex Tag 01MY; orbit-polynomial finite-group specialization of the invariant graded-ring argument.

proof.text: Both $M$ and its invariant open $V$ have admissible actions. Here is the affine-neighbourhood argument. For a finite orbit $E\subset V$, let $J$ be the homogeneous ideal generated by the positive-degree homogeneous $u$ with $D_+(u)\subset V$. The standard-open basis covers $V$, so $J$ cuts out its complement. The graded ideal $J\cap A_+$ is not contained in any of the finitely many homogeneous primes belonging to $E$: for each such prime take an element of $J$ outside it and multiply by a positive-degree element outside it. By [lem-sc-graded-prime-avoidance], choose a positive-degree homogeneous $t\in J$ avoiding all of $E$. Then $f=\prod_{h\in H}h(t)$ is homogeneous invariant, avoids all of $E$, and $D_+(f)=\bigcap_h D_+(h(t))\subset V$. It is affine by [lem-sc-proj-standard-open-basis]. These opens cover $V$. The same argument with $J=A_+$ covers $M$ by invariant affine standard opens. Thus [lem-per-admissible-quotient-affine-integral-charts] gives categorical quotients for $M$ and $V$, with geometric orbit fibres, invariant structure sheaf, and compatibility with invariant open restrictions.

source.place: Tag 00JS (lemma-graded-silly); admissible quotient as in Rydh Theorem 4.4, specialized to finite groups.

proof.text: For a positive-degree homogeneous $f\in C$, the inverse image of $D_+(f)\subset P$ under $r$ is $D_+(f)\subset M$, with coordinate ring $A_{(f),0}$, by [lem-per-finite-graded-proj-morphism]. One has $(A_{(f),0})^H=C_{(f),0}$. To prove this even with zero divisors, write an invariant element as $a/f^m$. Each $h(a)-a$ is killed by a power of $f$; a common exponent $k$ exists since $H$ is finite. Then $af^k$ is invariant and $a/f^m=(af^k)/f^{m+k}$ lies in $C_{(f),0}$. Localization preserves the inclusion $C\subseteq A$, proving the reverse injection. This equality is compatible with further homogeneous localization since both restriction maps send a fraction to that same fraction. The standard affine basis of [lem-sc-proj-standard-open-basis] therefore gives $\mathcal O_P=(r_*\mathcal O_M)^H$ as sheaves.

source.place: Tag 01MY, chart formula; degree-zero invariant localization calculation and gluing of the cited admissible quotients.

proof.text: On each affine chart above, apply [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-orbit-fibres] to $\coprod_{h\in H}D_+(f)\rightrightarrows D_+(f)$. The source is the fold map, the target restricts to the automorphism $h$ on its copy, and multiplication and inverse in $H$ give the groupoid structure. Both projections are finite locally free: on coordinate modules they are a finite free sum of copies of the chart ring, with the second sum identified by the automorphisms. Its equalizer is exactly $(A_{(f),0})^H=C_{(f),0}$. Thus the fibres of $r$ on points and on algebraically closed field-valued points are exactly $H$-orbits. The finite map $r$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], hence closed; together with surjectivity this makes its topology the quotient topology. The quotient $q_M:M\to Y$ supplied in Step 3 has that same orbit topology and invariant structure sheaf, by [lem-per-admissible-quotient-affine-integral-charts]. The unique homeomorphism $Y\cong P$ induced by the common orbit set identifies their sheaves, since both are the sheaf of invariant sections of $\mathcal O_M$ on the same inverse-image opens. It is therefore an isomorphism of schemes commuting with the quotient maps. In particular $r$ is categorical. The invariant-open restriction clause of the same node now shows that $Q=r(V)$ is open, $r^{-1}Q=V$, and $q=r|_V:V\to Q$ is its categorical geometric quotient. It is finite by restriction of the finite affine chart maps of $r$, and surjective. This restriction clause also proves the assertion for every invariant open of $V$.

source.place: Tag 03BL (lemma-points), for the constant finite-group action groupoid; compare the already cited admissible quotient by its orbit topology and invariant structure sheaf.

proof.text: The scheme $P=\operatorname{Proj}(C)$ is proper over $\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ by [lem-per-finite-type-graded-proj-proper], since Step 2 proved the required finite generation. In particular it is quasi-compact and locally of finite type. By [lem-trf-proj-qc-open-twist-ample] applied with the whole open $P$, a positive twist is an ample invertible module on $P$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ample-very-ample-immersion-affine-base] over $R_0$ to obtain an immersion $P\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_{R_0}$. This immersion is proper by [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target], since $P$ is proper over $R_0$ and projective space is separated (its properness follows from [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]). It is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed]. Because $R\twoheadrightarrow R_0$, the map $\operatorname{Spec}R_0\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion], and so is its base change $\mathbf P^n_{R_0}=\mathbf P^n_R\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}R_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The composite $P\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_R$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp]. The open $Q\subset P$ is $P\cap W$ for the open $W=\mathbf P^n_R\setminus(P\setminus Q)$, and $Q\to W$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; so $Q\to\mathbf P^n_R$ is an immersion.

source.place: Tag 01MW; morphisms.tex Tag 01VT; proper immersion criterion. All cited results apply over the affine degree-zero base, then the quotient base embeds closed into S.

proof.text: The invariant map $V\to B$ descends uniquely to $Q\to B$ by the categorical property proved in Step 5. Since $B\to S$ is quasi-projective, it is separated: a locally closed subscheme of projective space has closed diagonal, by restricting the diagonal of that separated projective space. The graph $Q\to Q\times_S B$ is consequently closed, as the pullback of this diagonal. The immersion $Q\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$ from Step 6 base changes to an immersion $Q\times_S B\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft]; it is a closed immersion into an open $U\subseteq\mathbf P^n_B$, and composing with the closed graph gives a closed immersion $Q\to U$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp], i.e. the desired finite projective-space immersion over $B$. The scheme $P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied over $\operatorname{Spec}R_0$; that base is Noetherian: ideals of $R_0$ are quotients of ideals of $R$, hence finitely generated, and [pqf-def-locnoeth] applies to its one affine chart. Its open $Q$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Every inverse image of an affine open of $B$ is therefore quasi-compact. The immersion $Q\to\mathbf P^n_B$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] and quasi-compact since $Q$ is Noetherian, so of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; $\mathbf P^n_B\to B$ is proper [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], hence separated and of finite type. Thus $Q\to B$ is of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. It is separated: the immersion is a monomorphism, so its diagonal is an isomorphism, and the diagonal of $Q$ over $B$ is the inverse image of the closed diagonal of $\mathbf P^n_B$.

source.place: Tag 01T5 (immersions locally of finite type); separated diagonal and graph calculation; Noetherian open-subscheme criterion.

proof.text: If $V\to B$ is projective, it is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]. We check universal closedness of $Q\to B$ directly. After any base change $B^\prime\to B$, the map $q^\prime:V\times_B B^\prime\to Q\times_B B^\prime$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. For any closed subset $Z$ of $Q\times_B B^\prime$, its inverse image under $q^\prime$ is closed, and its image in $B^\prime$ is closed since $V\to B$ is universally closed. Surjectivity makes this image precisely the image of $Z$. Thus $Q\to B$ is universally closed; it is separated and of finite type by Step 7, so proper by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The immersion $Q\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_B$ of Step 7 is proper by [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target] and [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] to make it a closed immersion. This is exactly projectivity in [def-kun-projective], with a finite number of coordinates.

source.place: Universal closedness descends through a surjection after every base change; proper immersion into finite projective space is closed.

proof.text: If $V$ is integral, the continuous surjection $q$ implies that $Q$ is nonempty and irreducible: two nonempty opens of $Q$ have nonempty inverse images in the irreducible space $V$, hence intersect. For an affine open $W\subset Q$, Step 5 identifies $q^{-1}W$ with an affine open of $V$, and $\mathcal O_Q(W)$ with the invariant subring of its coordinate ring. When $W$ is nonempty, that coordinate ring is a domain because $V$ is integral, and its invariant subring is a domain as well. Thus every nonempty affine open of $Q$ has a domain as its ring of functions, so $Q$ is integral in [def-pc-integral-scheme]. This proves the remaining clause without assuming that the action is faithful or tame.

source.place: Affine invariant charts of the cited quotient; elementary subring-of-a-domain argument.
